description.narrative: Myanmar faces severe threats to civilian safety due to intense armed conflict, widespread landmine contamination, internal displacement, and extreme weather. By early May, the displaced population reached 3 million, many in hard-to-reach areas without proper shelter or safe water, enduring extreme heat and monsoon conditions. The conflict has significantly escalated since October 2023, particularly in Rakhine, Kayin, Shan and Sagaing, resulting in a 50% increase in displacement over 6 months. The conflict resulted in 2,164 reported civilian casualties in 2023, including 745 fatalities, reflecting a 155% increase in casualties and deaths between 2022 and 2023. Oxfam, with partners GLAD and YCT, conducted rapid needs <(>&<)> market assessments in Rakhine and Southern Shan from May 25-27, 2024. They identified worsening water scarcity and disease, particularly acute watery diarrhea (AWD), stemming from sanitationand hygiene issues. In April, over 1,300 AWD cases were reported in Rakhine, with children under five being the most affected, including some fatalities. Displaced populations also face critical needs for shelter, NFIs <(>&<)> food. Markets are functional <(>&<)>can meet basic needs of people if given access to cash. According to UNOCHA Update #38, 3.9 million people still require WASH support, 2.25 million need food assistance, 2.2 million are in need of nutritional support, and 9 million need protection assistance, allof which remain unmet due to funding constraints and access issues. To address these unmet needs, Oxfam and its partners propose implementing WASH and MPC interventions, along with protection activities, to support 13,978 affected individuals. The MPC will enablerecipients to address their most pressing needs, while the WASH interventions will improve health conditions, and the protection activities will help prevent further harm. The project will be implemented in three townships in Rakhine and Shan following coordination with other DRA members

participating-org.narrative:
Oxfam great Britain is managing Oxfam in Myanmar. It has an office in Yangon since 2009 and operates in 5 townships as stipulated in its MOU with the Ministry of Agriculture and Irrigation.
Oxfam’s vision for Myanmar is for all citizens, including women and ethnic nationalities, to be able to enjoy their social, cultural, economic, civil and political rights. We believe it is possible for Myanmar to be led by a government that is responsive and accountable to its citizens; to have a political system everyone can be part of and have a dynamic private sector which works in the interests of the poorest. The focus of our work is now:
Empowering communities to exercise their own rights and increase their influence on local policies and resource allocation; promoting an accountable civil society which is able to drive pro-poor policies and equitable change. Building a responsive local government which can respond to the priorities of its people, engaging networks of communities, civil society and local government in order to work with a widerange of national and international actors. Increasing the participation of women in society, helping them to gain positions of leadership and to participate in decision making processes at all levels. Working towards a pro-poor private sector to ensure the private sector and the government adopt business practices and policies which benefit poor and vulnerable people.
To achieve our goals, the Oxfam Country strategy focuses on three thematic areas of work: Governance and Social Accountability, Economic Justice, and Humanitarian. Gender Equality is a core element in all programs, ensuring that we put women at the centre of everything we do.
